minecraftlodmod.configuration.title: Minecraft LOD — settings
minecraftlodmod.configuration.preset.too: Automatic picks one for your hardware. Custom uses the radius, detail and other values in the Quality tab. Changes apply when the next world is opened.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.fpsObjetiv: Used by auto-tuning in Custom mode; each preset has its own.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.autoAjuste: Measures every second whether the CPU or the GPU is the bottleneck and adjusts what relieves that side: GPU-bound, it splits more faces, hides more covered terrain and lowers the upscaling resolution; CPU-bound, it generates less at once and merges more faces. Only if that is not enough it lowers detail and radius, and restores them when there is headroom. It also reduces generation when there are stutters.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.personaliz: These values are only used with the Custom preset.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.umbralPx.t: Tolerated on-screen error: higher = less detail, more performance.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.colapsoDes: Level from which a uniform section is stored as a single voxel. 5 = never.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.radioServi: How much distant terrain each player may request. 0 = the preset radius.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.calibrar.t: Opens a fixed benchmark world, measures performance at 4 representative spots and saves the result as a Custom preset. Takes a few minutes.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.calibrar.e: Only available from the main menu.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.calibrar.c: Stops the running calibration without saving and returns to the configured quality.
minecraftlodmod.calibracion.resultado: Saved as Custom: LOD radius %s chunks
minecraftlodmod.calibracion.piso: Your hardware is at the lightest level; saved as Custom
minecraftlodmod.configuration.texturasLo: Draw distant terrain with the textures of the active resource pack; they simplify with distance. Off: flat colors.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.descartarC: Skip unlit faces (cave interiors, buried faces) in the LOD. Much less geometry; distant cave openings may show gaps.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.oclusionAm: Darkens corners, wall bases and under trees in the LOD, like vanilla smooth lighting. No GPU cost; slightly more geometry.
Draws the distant terrain. Turn it off to compare against vanilla; LOD generation keeps running.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.vanillaRed: With the LOD on, caps vanilla's render distance by preset (Minimum 5, Low 6, Medium 8, High 10, Ultra and Horizon 12 chunks) and the LOD draws the rest. Vanilla terrain is the most expensive thing to draw: noticeably more FPS and the server loads fewer chunks. Never raises the distance you chose in Video.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.pregenerar: Generates the world outward from you (like Chunky) so the LOD reaches far without exploring. Uses CPU and disk: chunks are saved to the world. Backs off by itself if the game slows down.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.radioPrege: 256 ≈ 200k chunks: 1-2 GB, tens of minutes. 1024 ≈ 3M: tens of GB, hours. 2048 ≈ 13M: hundreds of GB, days.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.ocultarTap: Skips building and drawing distant terrain hidden behind hills. Less work in mountainous areas; turn it off if something pops in late when climbing.
minecraftlodmod.comando.pregenerar.on: Pregeneration enabled (radius %s chunks). Check progress with /lod pregenerar
minecraftlodmod.comando.pregenerar.apaga: Pregeneration is off. Turn it on with /lod pregenerar on
minecraftlodmod.comando.pregenerar.estad: Pregenerating: ring %s of %s, %s new chunks (%s per second), %s in progress
minecraftlodmod.comando.pregenerar.compl: Pregeneration complete: radius %s chunks (%s new chunks)
minecraftlodmod.configuration.generacion: Estimates never-generated distant terrain straight from the world generator, without generating chunks: a multi-km horizon in minutes with no world disk usage. No structures or individual trees (forests show as canopy). Real chunks replace it as you explore or pregenerate.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.fsrEscalaP: 77 = Quality, 67 = Balanced, 59 = Performance, 50 = Ultra performance (AMD modes).
minecraftlodmod.configuration.hudRendimi: Shows at the top left the FPS (current, minimum and average since you joined the world) and CPU, RAM, GPU and VRAM usage, colored green, yellow and red as they approach 100%; FPS turn red below 30. Hidden with F1 or F3.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.hudDetalle: Second HUD line with the LOD's work: draw time, vertices, extraction and whether the limit is the CPU or the GPU. Off: only the first line.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.contratoVo: EXPERIMENTAL: with a shaderpack that ships the Voxy contract (voxy.json, e.g. Complementary), the LOD is drawn with the pack's own LOD code: the pack's lighting and fog on the LOD, without the edge fog (distant water is still opaque). Restart the game after changing it.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.sincroVert: EXPERIMENTAL (cubic chunks stage 1): the server only sends you the sections of each column that are close in height; whatever is far above or below (floating islands, mountains, deep caves) is drawn by the LOD. Less client memory, network and meshes; mostly noticeable in very tall worlds. Needs the mod on the server.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.distanciaV: 16-block sections above and below you that arrive with their real blocks. Lower = less memory and meshes; the rest is drawn by the LOD.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.logDepurac: Writes logs/minecraftlodmod-depuracion.log: one line per second with performance, position and LOD work, plus events (stutters, config changes, joining or leaving a world).
minecraftlodmod.hud.linea1: FPS %s  ·  %s ms (worst %s, 1%% low %s FPS)  ·  CPU game %s%% / system %s%%  ·  RAM %s/%s MB  ·  server %s ms
minecraftlodmod.hud.linea2: LOD %s ms · %s verts · %s pieces · %s MB · queue %s  ·  extraction %s/s (pend. %s)  ·  approx %s/s  ·  pregen %s
minecraftlodmod.configuration.escalado.t: Renders the world at a lower resolution and upscales it. FSR 1: spatial, any GPU. Temporal: built-in, accumulates frames, any GPU. XeSS: Intel, Windows, needs libxess.dll. DLSS: NVIDIA RTX, Windows, needs NVIDIA DLLs. Turns itself off with Fabulous, Iris or VulkanMod.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.invertirJi: If the image shimmers or stays blurry while standing still with XeSS or DLSS, try turning this on.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.vulkan.act: The game is using Vulkan. Click to go back to OpenGL on next launch.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.vulkan.se_: Next launch uses OpenGL. Click to cancel.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.vulkan.apa: The game uses OpenGL. Click to use Vulkan from next launch (this also turns off NeoForge's early loading window, which Vulkan does not support). No need to install VulkanMod separately: it is built in, and the standalone one cannot be installed at the same time.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.vulkan.se_: Next launch uses Vulkan. Click to cancel.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.vulkan.no_: Built-in Vulkan is only available on Windows and Linux.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.radioLodCh: How far the LOD reaches, in chunks. Only with the Custom preset.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.hilosGener: How many threads build LOD at once. More fills it faster but competes with the game. Only with the Custom preset.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.cacheRamMb: Memory for LOD in RAM before going to disk. Only with the Custom preset.
minecraftlodmod.pantalla.ayuda: Hover an option to see what it does and how much it costs. Changes stay yellow until applied; closing applies them. Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+S applies.
minecraftlodmod.pantalla.deshabilitada: Not available right now (depends on another option, such as the Custom preset).
minecraftlodmod.video.fullscreen: Fill the whole screen instead of a window. F11 also toggles it.
minecraftlodmod.video.resolucion: Fullscreen resolution. "Current" uses the desktop one; a lower one gives more FPS when the GPU is the limit, at the cost of sharpness.
minecraftlodmod.video.vsync: Syncs frames to the monitor refresh rate: no tearing, but a bit more latency and FPS tied to the monitor.
minecraftlodmod.video.framerateLimit: Frames per second cap. A cap near the monitor saves power and heat; LOD auto-tuning also uses it as the target when it is lower than the preset's.
minecraftlodmod.video.guiScale: Size of the interface (menus, inventory, HUD). Auto picks the largest that fits the window.
minecraftlodmod.video.gamma: Brightness of dark areas. It does not change world light, only how it looks.
minecraftlodmod.video.menuBackgroundBlur: Blur of the world behind menus. At 0 it is skipped, saving some GPU time.
minecraftlodmod.video.attackIndicator: Where to show attack charge: next to the crosshair, on the hotbar, or nowhere.
minecraftlodmod.video.showAutosaveIndica: Shows a notice when the world autosaves.
minecraftlodmod.video.fovEffectScale: How much the field of view changes when sprinting, with speed or slowness. The LOD adapts to the resulting FOV.
minecraftlodmod.video.screenEffectScale: Strength of screen distortions (nausea, Nether portal).
minecraftlodmod.video.renderDistance: Chunks Minecraft draws with real blocks. The LOD draws beyond that, so it can go down without losing the horizon: the biggest FPS gain.
minecraftlodmod.video.simulationDistance: Chunks around you where the world runs (mobs, crops, redstone). Costs CPU, not GPU.
minecraftlodmod.video.prioritizeChunkUpd: When chunks are rebuilt after placing or breaking blocks: in the background (smoother) or in the same frame (no flicker, possible stutter).
minecraftlodmod.video.graphicsMode: Fast: opaque leaves and fewer effects. Fancy: transparent leaves. Fabulous: correct transparency, much more expensive, and disables LOD upscaling.
minecraftlodmod.video.ambientOcclusion: Soft shadows in the corners of nearby blocks. The LOD has its own option under LOD Quality.
minecraftlodmod.video.particles: Amount of particles (smoke, rain, hits). Many particles cost CPU.
minecraftlodmod.video.biomeBlendRadius: How gradual grass, leaf and water colors blend between biomes. High values make chunk building slower.
minecraftlodmod.video.entityShadows: Round shadow under mobs and items.
minecraftlodmod.video.entityDistanceScal: Distance at which mobs and items are drawn, relative to normal.
minecraftlodmod.video.mipmapLevels: Smaller texture versions for distant surfaces: less shimmering and moiré. Changing it reloads textures.
minecraftlodmod.video.shaders.tooltip: Opens the Iris shader pack screen. The LOD is drawn with the pack's terrain.
minecraftlodmod.video.vulkanmod.tooltip: Opens the integrated VulkanMod settings (its own video options). Its LOD button comes back here.
minecraftlodmod.video.original.tooltip: Opens Minecraft's unchanged video settings screen, in case another mod adds something there this one does not show. Leaving it comes back here.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.texturasCo: Far terrain voxels span several blocks. On: grass (and snowy grass, mycelium, podzol) sides get the green band only on their top row and dirt below, like a terrain cut. Off: the texture repeats every block, showing a grass line per block.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.nieblaLluv: With rain or thunder the LOD gets more haze and a smaller radius (down to half): what the fog hides is not drawn. Less GPU load while it rains.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.nieblaSinD: Fog where the LOD has no data yet (unloaded or still building): in each direction the fog ends where the missing part starts, so no hard edges or holes are visible.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.fundidoNiv: When an area of the LOD changes detail level, the old and new meshes cross-fade with a dither for under half a second instead of popping, and the old one stays until the new one is ready (no holes). Small cost: a few extra draws while it fades.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.oclusionPa: Soft shadow in valleys, at the foot of mountains and under trees in the LOD, computed on the image (SSAO, like Voxy). Adds depth to distant terrain. Costs some GPU per LOD pixel; turn it off on weak integrated graphics.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.neblinaAtm: Distant terrain fades towards the sky colour with distance, like real air. 0 = none, 1 = the horizon becomes the sky colour. The LOD edge always ends inside the fog. No performance cost.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.nubesLejan: Minecraft cuts clouds off a few hundred blocks away. On: they continue with the same shape and motion as far as the LOD reaches, blending into the sky at the horizon. Not available with Vulkan or shader packs (they draw their own clouds).
Curves the distant terrain like a planet's surface: far terrain drops and hides behind the horizon. It starts where normal terrain ends, so there is no step.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.radioCurva: Planet size (1 block = 1 meter). Earth 1:1 gives a realistic, subtle curve; a small planet makes it very visible.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.horizonteR: The LOD radius no longer comes from the preset: it is computed from eye height above sea level and the planet radius, as far as the real horizon would be (plus a hill behind it). Higher means farther. Earth 1:1 can ask for thousands of blocks: approximate generation helps. Auto-tuning still trims it if performance falls short.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.pixelesMax: LOD detail is chosen by how much of the screen each voxel covers, not by distance: with this cap no voxel looks bigger than this, however far or large it is (a 1 km voxel at 100 km looks as small as an 8-block one at 800). Neither the preset nor auto-tuning exceeds it: if performance falls short, they trim the radius. Lower = sharper and more expensive.
minecraftlodmod.configuration.escaladoSo: Upscaling only if it gains FPS

Every 2 minutes it measures a few seconds with and without upscaling and keeps it on only if frames are faster. Lowering the resolution only helps when the GPU is busy drawing pixels; when the CPU is the limit (most common in Minecraft), upscaling costs and turns itself off. The result goes to the log.
